newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE Brent weak but look for a correction.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE Brent weak but look for a correction.

text.p: ARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20

* Brent crude futures remain technically weak but the market at these lower levels may begin to find fundamental support. * Analysts look for corrective strength lasting more than a day in the area $17.32-$17.90.

IPE Brent crude futures remain technically weak with fresh downside targets presenting themselves daily, but technicals aside the market at these lower levels may begin to find fundamental support, analysts said.
Tom James at Credit Lyonaiss Rouse in Singapore said that despite the market's recent slide from $19 it was now looking more comfortable in the $17.50-$18.50 a barrel range.
He said that while pure technicals looked rather sick the current low crude prices would draw fresh demand from the Far East, providing fundamental support.
"We were a bit overpriced at $19 but the $17.50-$18.50 range looks more comfortable, fundamentals started the recent fall and fundamentals will probably stop it," James said.

U.S. funds liquidated long positions after the market fell through $19 at the beginning of June and were also seen selling in late trade Wednesday in order to protect profits on what are now fairly large short positions held around $18.25-50 a barrel range, brokers said.

Al Graham at Elliott Wave International, Gainesville, Georgia said, "The next event to look for is that of corrective strength lasting more than a day that starts from probably not all that much under $17.32 and carries back to near or a little above $17.90. After this upcoming bounce, we must again fall to another new low to finish the decline pattern from $20.60.
IPE Brokers said sentiment remained cautious about a rebound.
However, they said the next major low on the charts was $16.75 -- the low of May 20, 1996. Since that was some distance away, it might tempt players to cut back short positions ahead of the weekend.
Brent futures were slightly firmer on Thursday in Asia but sentiment remained cautious after two successive days of fresh 13-month lows.
July Brent was last traded on SIMEX at $17.45 per barrel up 10 cents from London's Wednesday settlement.
Brent on the IPE ended down 15 cents at $17.35 and just three cents above after the intraday low, the lowest since May 20, 1996.
NYMEX crude rebounded in overnight ACCESS trade was last traded at $18.64, up 11 cents from the New York close.

Graham advised caution for IPE gas oil. "The bounce from $161.25 is corrective and could easily finish above $164 over the next day or so, but will be followed by another drop under $161.25," he said.
June IPE gas oil ended up 75 cents at $162.25 a tonne on Wednesday.
--Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
